capabilities.text: Start from the supported count and variance review. The adjustment should express an authorized conclusion, not merely repeat the most recent number someone entered while investigating a mismatch.

capabilities.title: Separate approval and posting
capabilities.text: Recognize the decision to approve and the action that changes recorded stock as distinct steps. This gives managers a clearer point of accountability for the correction.

capabilities.title: Retain a linked change
capabilities.text: Keep the resulting stock movement connected to its reviewed variance. A later investigation should be able to explain the correction without losing the count evidence behind it.

faq.q: Can we just replace the quantity with the number we counted?
faq.a: Use the supported count, review and posting process instead of an unexplained overwrite. The observed amount, timing, approval and resulting movement all contribute to an understandable correction.

faq.q: What if sales continue while we review the count?
faq.a: Review the relevant stock activity and timing before posting. A count is an observation at a point in the workflow, so ongoing movements need consideration when the store decides how to correct its records.

count-adjustments.intro: When stock records need correcting, the reason should survive the correction. Count adjustments turn a reviewed inventory variance into a linked stock change, giving the owner a clearer account of how the new quantity was reached and authorized.
count-adjustments.demoQuestion: Can we explain a corrected stock figure from its count evidence and approval?

explanation: This is particularly important during receiving, when questionable plants or damaged containers can otherwise disappear into the general stock conversation. Recording the appropriate condition keeps that uncertainty visible while staff investigate the delivery and decide what should happen to the goods.

The physical routine still matters. The team needs to separate and identify the actual items, not only choose a condition on screen. Returning goods to sellable status is another authorized decision, with a reason that reflects what staff have verified about their current condition.

capabilities.title: Record the condition distinction
capabilities.text: Use the supported damaged or quarantine category where the goods need review. Their physical presence should not automatically make them part of a confident ready-to-sell promise.

capabilities.title: Support delivery review
capabilities.text: Keep questionable received quantities identifiable while the team checks the delivery. That makes it easier to discuss the actual condition with the supplier and the person reviewing the receipt.

capabilities.title: Require a deliberate release
capabilities.text: Treat a later return to sellable condition as an authorized decision. The recorded category and the physical handling should change only when the team has reviewed what is appropriate.

faq.q: Does the software physically separate damaged plants for us?
faq.a: No. Staff still need to identify and separate the actual goods. The recorded condition supports that routine but cannot prevent a damaged item being placed on a selling bench without proper handling.

faq.q: Should damaged goods always be recorded as a complete loss?
faq.a: Not automatically. Condition review and a documented known-loss event answer different questions. Follow the store's decision about the goods and use the workflow for the actual outcome.

damaged-stock.intro: A tray can be present in the building and still be unsuitable for sale. Damaged-stock handling gives the team a recorded distinction between goods being reviewed and goods considered ready, supporting a clearer decision about condition before customers are promised an item.
damaged-stock.demoQuestion: Can we keep a questionable delivery quantity separate from stock we can promise to customers?

explanation: Receipts, losses, transfers and adjustments represent different kinds of work. Reviewing the relevant movements helps the team ask the next practical question: which event explains the change, and which physical activity may still need checking? The history is evidence of what was recorded, not proof of unrecorded handling.

This is useful when several people touch the same stock during a busy day. Rather than assuming the latest count reveals the cause of every difference, review the sequence and its sources. Keep the investigation separate from the authorized correction that may follow.

capabilities.title: Review the quantity trail
capabilities.text: Look beyond the current total to the recorded activity behind it. This gives a manager a more focused basis for discussing a difference with receiving, sales or stock-handling staff.

capabilities.title: Distinguish movement reasons
capabilities.text: Keep different operations understandable in the review. A receipt, transfer or count correction should not all be interpreted as the same kind of stock change simply because the net amount is similar.

capabilities.title: Find the next question
capabilities.text: Use retained movement context to guide investigation. Where actual handling was never recorded, the team still needs to establish what happened before choosing an appropriate correction.

faq.q: Will the history explain every physical discrepancy?
faq.a: Only recorded activity is represented. The history can narrow an investigation, but missing handling, an incorrect observation or goods moved without the supported record still require staff review.

faq.q: Can we fix stock by changing an old movement?
faq.a: Use the appropriate supported correction workflow rather than erasing the explanation of earlier activity. Count adjustments and other authorized remedies should preserve a clear connection to the records being reviewed.

stock-movement-history.intro: A stock number tells you where the records stand. Movement history helps explain how they got there. Owners can review recorded activity behind a product's quantity, giving a discrepancy investigation a more useful starting point than a total with no context.
stock-movement-history.demoQuestion: Can we trace a stock change through receipts, losses or a reviewed count correction?

explanation: The value is in the handoffs. The source needs to know what was sent; the destination needs to confirm what actually arrived. Keeping those events distinct is especially important when a delivery is received in parts or a quantity remains between the two locations.

Owners should review this alongside store and register setup. Correct locations and staff authority give the transfer its intended context, while the physical team remains responsible for loading, checking and receiving the actual goods. A posted transfer is not a substitute for counting the delivery at the destination.

capabilities.title: Record both ends
capabilities.text: Keep the source and destination tied to the movement. This helps each store understand its role instead of relying on separate notes that may describe the same transfer differently.

capabilities.title: Separate shipping and receiving
capabilities.text: Recognize dispatch and arrival as different events. Goods should not be treated as confirmed at the destination merely because the source recorded that they left.

capabilities.title: Review partial arrivals
capabilities.text: Use the transfer evidence to understand quantities received and still outstanding. That gives the team a clearer way to investigate a delivery arriving in stages.

faq.q: Is transferring stock the same as making a retail sale?
faq.a: No. A transfer moves goods within the configured store operation and needs its own source, transit and destination records. It should not be interpreted as customer revenue simply because stock leaves one location.

faq.q: Can the receiving store confirm only part of a transfer?
faq.a: The supported transfer process retains partial-receipt evidence. Staff should confirm what actually arrived and review the remaining in-transit quantity instead of marking the whole transfer received prematurely.

inter-store-transfers.intro: Moving plants between stores should leave a clear record at both ends. Inter-store transfers give the team a defined sequence for requesting, approving, shipping and receiving goods, so the journey can be reviewed without confusing it with a customer sale.
inter-store-transfers.demoQuestion: Can we transfer plants between two configured stores and record a partial arrival?

explanation: This is a status-review question within the transfer journey. Compare what was shipped with what the receiving team has confirmed, then investigate the remainder. That is more useful than assuming every dispatched plant is already available to the destination's customers.

The record depends on the physical handoffs being posted accurately. A forgotten shipment or receipt leaves the review incomplete. Agree who confirms each stage, especially when more than one person or vehicle is involved, so the retained transit information describes the actual movement as closely as possible.

capabilities.title: Distinguish goods on the way
capabilities.text: Keep shipped quantities separate from confirmed arrivals. This supports a more realistic availability conversation at the destination while the transfer remains physically in progress.

capabilities.title: Review outstanding receipts
capabilities.text: Compare the transfer's recorded shipment and receiving events. The difference helps the manager focus on what still needs confirmation rather than treating the transfer as a single completed action.

capabilities.title: Support handoff accountability
capabilities.text: Use the record to discuss which physical stage has been confirmed and which has not. Staff posting habits remain essential to making the transit view useful for the owner.

faq.q: Does shipped stock become available at the destination immediately?
faq.a: Do not assume that. The receiving team needs to confirm arrival through the supported transfer workflow, and the physical condition and quantity should be checked before promises are made to customers.

faq.q: What if the goods have arrived but still appear in transit?
faq.a: Review whether the receiving event has been recorded correctly. The status reflects the retained shipment and receipt evidence; it does not automatically detect the physical truck's arrival at the store.

in-transit-stock.intro: Goods on the truck occupy a different place in the business from goods ready on a selling bench. In-transit stock makes that distinction visible in the transfer record, helping owners understand what has left one store but is not yet confirmed at another.
in-transit-stock.demoQuestion: Can we distinguish goods on the truck from goods confirmed at the receiving store?

explanation: A saved record is useful because it gives repeat buying a consistent starting point. Staff can choose the intended supplier and review its details before moving into the purchase order. That is particularly helpful when someone covers buying duties for a colleague who normally holds the information in their head.

Good supplier records still need attention. Contacts, pack arrangements and commercial details can change, and a blank field should remain an unanswered question. Review what is current before relying on it, rather than letting a familiar supplier name stand in for verified ordering information.

capabilities.title: Keep repeat details accessible
capabilities.text: Retain the supplier information already recorded by the store. Staff can begin a new purchasing task from that shared reference instead of hunting through previous emails for every basic detail.

capabilities.title: Choose the intended relationship
capabilities.text: Select the correct supplier before preparing the order. Similar trading names or multiple contacts deserve a quick check so the buying conversation begins with the right organization.

capabilities.title: Review what has changed
capabilities.text: Treat the saved record as maintained business information. Check that contact and purchasing details remain suitable when the supplier changes its arrangements or a new staff member takes over the task.

faq.q: Will the system find supplier contact details we have never entered?
faq.a: No. Saved suppliers make recorded information reusable; they do not invent missing addresses, phone numbers or commercial arrangements. Confirm those details through your normal supplier relationship before depending on them.

faq.q: Does choosing a saved supplier place an order with them?
faq.a: No. Selecting the supplier starts the internal purchasing workflow. Preparing, approving and actually communicating an order remain distinct steps that the store needs to manage appropriately.

saved-suppliers.intro: The next order should begin with what your store already knows about the supplier. Saved suppliers keep recorded contact and purchasing details available to the buying team, reducing the need to reconstruct the same relationship every time another order is prepared.
saved-suppliers.demoQuestion: Can another team member start a repeat order using our maintained supplier information?

explanation: The record gives receiving something concrete to compare against later. Instead of asking whether a delivery looks roughly like the conversation with the grower, staff can review the intended goods and their recorded purchasing context. Confirm the units carefully, especially where supplier packaging differs from retail selling.

A completed internal order record does not mean the supplier has accepted it. Keep preparation, approval and supplier communication understandable as separate business steps. Owners can then use the purchase order to organize the decision without making an unsupported assumption about what has actually been ordered externally.

capabilities.title: Prepare a coherent buying record
capabilities.text: Bring the proposed supplier items, quantities and expected costs together. This gives the reviewer a clear description of the intended purchase before the business commits to the next step.

capabilities.title: Review purchasing units
capabilities.text: Check what each supplier quantity represents. The meaning of a tray, pack or case needs to be understood before its expected goods can be compared with a later delivery.

capabilities.title: Support later receiving
capabilities.text: Use the recorded order as a reference when goods arrive. The receiving decision should reflect the delivery actually checked, including differences that need their own explanation.

faq.q: Will creating the purchase order automatically email or place it with the supplier?
faq.a: No. This feature creates the internal order record. Follow your normal approved supplier communication process and confirm the commercial commitment rather than assuming the software has dispatched it automatically.

faq.q: Does the expected cost prove what the final delivery will cost?
faq.a: No. It is the cost context prepared for the order. Actual delivered quantities, exceptions and recorded landed costs still need review before the store interprets the received goods' cost.

purchase-orders.intro: A buying decision is easier to manage when everyone can see what the store intends to order. Purchase orders bring supplier lines, quantities, units and expected costs into a clear internal record the team can prepare and review together.
purchase-orders.demoQuestion: Can we prepare an order that the owner and receiving team can both understand?

explanation: This allows the owner to delegate preparation without making authority ambiguous. A team member can gather the intended supplier lines and expected quantities, while the appropriate reviewer considers whether the order reflects the store's plans. The approval step is a deliberate decision, not an assumption attached to staff access.

The external supplier relationship still needs its own confirmation. An internal approval does not establish acceptance of terms or guarantee a delivery. Review staff permissions and the actual ordering routine together so the team understands what approval changes and which business steps must still happen afterwards.

capabilities.title: Separate preparation from authority
capabilities.text: Let the order's preparation and approval represent different responsibilities. This helps the owner decide where buying work can be shared without silently granting every participant purchasing authority.

capabilities.title: Review the proposed commitment
capabilities.text: Consider the supplier lines and quantities before approving the internal order. The useful outcome is a documented buying decision that receiving and management can refer back to later.

capabilities.title: Align access with store policy
capabilities.text: Configure the staff authority that supports the intended review process. The team should understand who can prepare, who can approve and when a question needs the owner's attention.

faq.q: Can a seasonal buyer prepare an order without approving it?
faq.a: That is the intended separation to review through your configured staff permissions. The store should confirm the actual roles and approval workflow before delegating live purchasing responsibility.

faq.q: Does an approved order prove the supplier agreed to it?
faq.a: No. Internal approval and external supplier acceptance are different events. Confirm the order and any commercial terms through the store's normal supplier communication process before assuming the goods are committed.

purchase-approvals.intro: The person preparing a grower order may not be the person authorized to approve the purchase. Purchase approvals give that distinction a place in the workflow, so proposed buying can be reviewed before it becomes an approved internal commitment.
purchase-approvals.demoQuestion: Can one staff member prepare an order while the owner retains approval authority?

explanation: The receiving decision begins at the truck or unloading area. Staff compare what is present with the intended order, then confirm the quantities they have checked. An expected future delivery should not be recorded as stock simply because it shares the same purchase order.

This creates a clearer conversation for the next shift and the next truck. The owner can distinguish a partly fulfilled order from a fully received one, while exceptions such as shortages or substitutions keep their own reasons. The record should explain the delivery, not smooth away its inconvenient details.

capabilities.title: Confirm the delivered portion
capabilities.text: Record the quantities staff actually received and checked. This keeps today's stock decision tied to today's physical delivery rather than to the supplier's original promise for the whole order.

capabilities.title: Retain the order remainder
capabilities.text: Keep the undelivered quantity understandable after the first receipt. The team needs a clear reference for what is still expected when another delivery or supplier conversation follows.

capabilities.title: Review differences separately
capabilities.text: Treat an actual shortage, substitution or extra item as an exception needing review. A staged delivery and an unexplained mismatch may look similar but require different business decisions.

faq.q: Should we mark the whole order received if the rest is coming tomorrow?
faq.a: No. Confirm the actual delivered portion and retain the remainder. Stock should not imply that undelivered goods are already present simply because another shipment is expected soon.

faq.q: What if the supplier later says the remainder will never arrive?
faq.a: Review the outstanding quantity through the supported shortage or remainder-cancellation workflow. Preserve the receipts already recorded while resolving the part of the commitment that is still open.

partial-receiving.intro: A grower may fill one order over more than one delivery. Partial receiving lets the team record the goods that actually arrived while keeping the undelivered remainder visible, instead of forcing an all-or-nothing answer onto a staged shipment.
partial-receiving.demoQuestion: Can we receive one truckload while keeping the rest of the supplier order open?

explanation: The first job is to establish what the goods are. A supplier substitution may be commercially acceptable but still represent a different product or quantity relationship. Confirm identity, units and condition before the delivery is treated as ordinary sellable stock in the receiving workflow.

A useful exception record also helps the owner continue the supplier conversation. Staff can explain the observed difference without relying on someone remembering what arrived last week. The recorded reason supports that discussion; it does not replace agreement with the supplier about the commercial outcome.

capabilities.title: Explain the mismatch
capabilities.text: Retain the reason for an overage, shortage or substitution. A clear exception helps later reviewers understand why the confirmed receipt differs from the original purchasing expectation.

capabilities.title: Verify the actual goods
capabilities.text: Check the product, pack relationship and condition being received. Accepting a substitute should be a conscious review of the item rather than an assumed equivalence based on similar wording.

capabilities.title: Keep supplier decisions separate
capabilities.text: Document the physical delivery while confirming commercial arrangements through the normal supplier relationship. Recording an exception does not, by itself, establish an agreed credit or revised purchase price.

faq.q: Can we treat a larger pot size as the original item because the plant name matches?
faq.a: Not without reviewing the actual product and unit relationship. A substitution needs a retained reason and correct product identification before the receiving record can accurately describe the goods accepted.

faq.q: Does recording a shortage automatically settle the supplier's invoice?
faq.a: No. It records the observed receiving difference. Invoice questions, credits and the commercial agreement still require the store's normal review with the supplier and the person responsible for accounts.

receiving-exceptions.intro: Extra trays, missing items and a substituted pot size all deserve an explanation at receiving. Receiving exceptions let the team retain those differences with a reason, so the store's record describes the delivery it actually handled rather than the order it hoped to receive.
receiving-exceptions.demoQuestion: Can we document a substituted item without pretending it is identical to the original order?

explanation: Start with the cost evidence you actually have. The supported workflow allocates recorded components across received goods, rather than leaving the entire charge disconnected from the delivery. Staff still need to check the input amount and the goods included in the review before relying on the result.

This is operational cost context, with an important boundary. A recorded allocation is not automatically a verified inventory valuation or a complete cost-of-goods-sold figure. Keep the bookkeeper involved in how those numbers are interpreted, especially when they inform later margin or accounting decisions.

capabilities.title: Include recorded delivery costs
capabilities.text: Bring eligible freight or duty components into the supported receipt-cost review. This helps the owner see cost information that would otherwise remain separate from the goods received.

capabilities.title: Review the allocation scope
capabilities.text: Check which received goods the component belongs to before using the allocation. A sound calculation still depends on an accurate amount and an appropriate set of products.

capabilities.title: Keep financial meaning clear
capabilities.text: Distinguish operational landed-cost information from accountant-reviewed valuation and cost of goods sold. The resulting number is useful when staff understand what evidence it includes and what it does not establish.

faq.q: Does allocating freight automatically tell us the profit on every product?
faq.a: No. Profit analysis depends on the appropriate revenue and reviewed cost evidence. Receipt allocations provide context, but should not be substituted for a verified cost-of-goods-sold basis without the required accounting review.

faq.q: What should we check before allocating a delivery charge?
faq.a: Confirm the actual component amount, the receiving records it relates to and the goods in scope. Review unusual charges with the person responsible for purchasing or accounts before relying on the result.

freight-and-landed-costs.intro: The grower's item price may be only part of what it costs to bring goods into the store. Freight and landed-cost allocation give recorded delivery-related components a place alongside the received products, supporting a fuller cost conversation for the owner.
flow: Review the received goods in scope
freight-and-landed-costs.demoQuestion: Can we explain how a recorded freight charge is allocated across a reviewed receipt?

explanation: The relationship belongs to the verified supplier item and product variant. A pack name is not enough: different growers or products can use familiar packaging words for different amounts. Review the actual contents and recorded ratio, especially when an existing supplier changes its specification.

Keep the retail side separate. What arrives in a supplier pack may later be sold individually or through another configured option. Owners need those buying and selling relationships to agree with the physical goods, without assuming that a supplier tray automatically defines the customer's purchase unit.

capabilities.title: Translate supplier quantities
capabilities.text: Use the recorded pack-to-product relationship when reviewing received goods. This makes the supplier's purchasing unit understandable in terms of the store's intended stock quantity.

capabilities.title: Verify the mapped variant
capabilities.text: Confirm which product the supplier pack actually contains. The correct numerical ratio is not enough if the receiving relationship points to the wrong size or product option.

capabilities.title: Recheck changed packaging
capabilities.text: Review conversions when suppliers alter tray contents or specifications. Keeping a familiar vendor reference should not silently preserve a quantity relationship that no longer matches the goods.

faq.q: Is the supplier's pack size automatically the same as our retail flat?
faq.a: No. Receiving and customer selling are different relationships. Review each configured conversion against the actual goods and the way your store purchases and sells that product.

faq.q: What happens if a supplier changes the number of plants in a tray?
faq.a: Review the supplier mapping and conversion before confirming new receipts. A familiar product name or code does not prove that the previous quantity relationship remains correct for the new packaging.

supplier-pack-conversions.intro: Your supplier may count trays while your store counts plants. Supplier pack conversions define that relationship before receiving, so the quantity on the grower's paperwork can become an understandable stock quantity without a last-minute calculation at the unloading area.
supplier-pack-conversions.demoQuestion: Can we receive a grower's trays into the correct number of stock units?

explanation: The aim is to reduce the blank-screen moment after someone notices a stock concern. Existing information can help the buyer get oriented, but the team still decides whether to order, from whom and in what quantity. The suggestion is a starting point for that decision.

Owners should review the whole path, including message delivery and the protected destination. A useful email link is not automatic purchasing or demand forecasting. Demonstrate how the buyer checks current supplier arrangements and availability before turning historical context into a proposed new commitment.

capabilities.title: Connect the alert to buying
capabilities.text: Use the eligible message's order destination to move into the supported purchasing workflow. This gives the person acting on the alert a clearer next step than starting from an unrelated screen.

capabilities.title: Bring relevant history forward
capabilities.text: Review saved supplier and eligible receipt-based information as context. Prior purchasing activity can reduce repeated lookup work without becoming authority to repeat an old decision unchanged.

capabilities.title: Keep the buyer in control
capabilities.text: Confirm present needs, quantities and supplier arrangements before preparing the order. The workflow supports judgment; it does not automatically place a purchase because a message identified low recorded stock.

faq.q: Does a low-stock alert automatically order more plants?
faq.a: No. It leads into a reviewed new-order process. The buyer remains responsible for confirming need, supplier, quantities and the approval or communication steps that the store requires.

faq.q: Will the email link work without setting up delivery?
faq.a: Message delivery and the relevant protected workflow need configuration and verification. Review the actual recipient and destination during setup rather than treating an available template as evidence that alerts are being delivered.

low-stock-reorder-starting-points.intro: An alert becomes more useful when it leads to the next job. Low-stock reorder starting points connect an eligible message to the new-order workflow, where the buyer can review relevant supplier information and receipt-based suggestions before preparing another purchase.
low-stock-reorder-starting-points.demoQuestion: Can a low-stock message take our buyer to a useful order starting point?

explanation: The benefit is reduced re-entry, not an assumption that yesterday's arrangement still applies. A prior receipt can show how the store bought the item before. The buyer then checks whether the supplier, packaging and cost remain suitable for the proposed purchase today.

That review is especially important during seasonal changes. A familiar product may arrive in a different pack or at a changed price. Owners can retain the convenience of historical defaults while keeping the current buying decision explicit, with ordinary approvals still governing what happens next.

capabilities.title: Reuse eligible context
capabilities.text: Begin from suitable historical supplier and receipt information where the supported defaults apply. This helps the buyer avoid repeatedly reconstructing details already recorded by the store.

capabilities.title: Check the pack relationship
capabilities.text: Review whether the supplier item and packaging are unchanged. A prior quantity or cost makes sense only within the product and pack relationship that originally supported it.

capabilities.title: Confirm current commercial details
capabilities.text: Treat the historical cost as a reference for review, not a current offer from the supplier. The new purchasing decision still needs today's confirmed arrangement and the store's normal approval process.

faq.q: Can we treat the previous receipt cost as the supplier's current price?
faq.a: No. A historical amount shows the recorded earlier purchase context. Confirm the current commercial arrangement before relying on that value in a new order or presenting it as a live supplier quote.

faq.q: Why might a familiar product not receive the same defaults?
faq.a: Defaults depend on eligible source and pack relationships. A changed supplier mapping or packaging can make previous details unsuitable, which is why the buyer should review the proposed starting information.

previous-order-defaults.intro: Repeat buying should not require rebuilding every detail from memory. Previous-order defaults give the buyer eligible historical supplier, pack and cost information to review, helping another order begin with useful context from the store's own recorded activity.
flow: Confirm the current pack and cost
previous-order-defaults.demoQuestion: Can we start a repeat purchase from history while checking that its details still apply?

explanation: The assistant prepares possibilities; the receiving team verifies them. Compare the suggested product matches and quantities with both the document and the actual goods. An attractive transcription is not enough where a tray is short, a pot size is substituted or the physical condition needs review.

This keeps automation in a helpful supporting role. The manager can review the proposed information before the normal receiving confirmation changes stock. Include an imperfect packing slip in the demonstration so your team sees how uncertain or incorrect suggestions are handled, not only how a clear document is read.

capabilities.title: Start with the approved order
capabilities.text: Choose an approved purchase order before uploading the delivery document. The assistant uses that order’s context to prepare suggestions for the receiving team to check against the goods.

capabilities.title: Review suggested matches
capabilities.text: Check the proposed product identity and quantities against the goods received. Staff remain responsible for resolving ambiguous names, different pack sizes and other details the document alone cannot establish.

capabilities.title: Confirm through receiving
capabilities.text: Use the reviewed receiving workflow for the stock decision. An uploaded image or assistant suggestion does not by itself authorize the store to treat goods as correctly received.

faq.q: Will uploading the packing slip automatically add everything to stock?
faq.a: No. Staff must review the suggestions and confirm the receipt through the workflow. The actual quantities, product matches and condition need human checking before the receiving decision is completed.

faq.q: Can the assistant make mistakes with a supplier's document?
faq.a: Yes. Document quality, wording and product relationships can create uncertainty. Use the suggestions as preparation, then compare them with the actual goods and correct any issue before confirming the receipt.

photo-assisted-receiving.intro: Start with an approved purchase order, then upload the supplier’s packing slip. Photo-assisted receiving suggests draft details within that order’s context, so staff can focus on checking the actual delivery rather than beginning the review with a blank record.
flow: Upload and review the packing slip
photo-assisted-receiving.demoQuestion: Can we open an approved order, upload an imperfect packing slip and review the goods before stock changes?

explanation: The confirmation is what makes the lookup useful. Similar names, shared contact information or an old detail can produce ambiguity. Staff should compare the available record with the customer's answer rather than selecting the first plausible result simply to move the line along.

At the same time, an ordinary anonymous sale can remain anonymous. Lookup supports the situations where identifying a customer is appropriate; it is not a reason to collect unnecessary details from everyone. Keep the receipt and any optional marketing preference as separate customer choices in their own supported workflows.

capabilities.title: Find an existing record
capabilities.text: Search the supported recorded name, phone or email when the customer provides it. This gives staff a practical route to a profile that may already belong to the person being served.

capabilities.title: Confirm the intended person
capabilities.text: Check the result before using it for the sale or account conversation. A familiar name is a useful clue, but it should not substitute for a reasonable identity confirmation.

capabilities.title: Avoid unnecessary new profiles
capabilities.text: Use the existing record where it has been confirmed. When no customer attachment is needed, ordinary anonymous checkout can continue without turning the purchase into a compulsory data-collection exercise.

faq.q: Does every shopper have to provide their name or email?
faq.a: No. Ordinary anonymous sales do not require a customer record. Use customer lookup where the task calls for it and keep receipt delivery and marketing permission distinct from identifying the sale's customer.

faq.q: Should a cashier merge two similar profiles while checking out?
faq.a: A similar result is not enough to confirm a duplicate. The reviewed customer-merge workflow is a separate job, with checks that protect identity and retained history from an incorrect combination.

customer-lookup.intro: A regular customer should not need a new profile every time they return. Customer lookup helps staff find an existing record using the information the shopper provides, then confirm the intended person before attaching that identity to the purchase.
customer-lookup.demoQuestion: Can we find a repeat customer without creating another profile or requiring every shopper to register?

explanation: The work begins with evidence, not resemblance. Similar names or contact details can point toward a question without proving that two profiles belong to the same person. Review the candidates and any conflicting identities or trade-account relationships before deciding a merge is appropriate.

For the owner, this is a data-quality decision with service consequences. A cleaner customer record can make later lookup less confusing, but a mistaken merge can attach the wrong history or account context. Keep the review deliberate and separate from a cashier's immediate need to finish a sale.

capabilities.title: Review suspected duplicates
capabilities.text: Examine the candidate profiles before deciding they represent the same customer. The goal is to resolve a verified duplication, not simply reduce the number of records in a list.

capabilities.title: Preserve customer history
capabilities.text: Use the supported merge workflow rather than deleting a profile to make it disappear. Retained history matters when the team later reviews purchases, account context or the reason records were combined.

capabilities.title: Respect blocking conflicts
capabilities.text: Treat incompatible identities or trade-account relationships as issues requiring review. A convenient merge should not silently override evidence that the two records may need to remain distinct.

faq.q: Can we merge profiles because they have the same surname?
faq.a: No. A shared surname is not sufficient evidence of one customer. Review the available identity information and account context before confirming that the records are eligible duplicates.

faq.q: What if both records have a trade account or conflicting linked identity?
faq.a: Those relationships can block a merge. Resolve the actual conflict through the appropriate review rather than assuming that a similar name allows one profile's account or history to be absorbed into the other.

customer-duplicate-review.intro: Duplicate customer profiles make a familiar person look like several unrelated records. Customer duplicate review gives managers a considered way to confirm an eligible match and bring those records together while retaining the history the business still needs to understand.
customer-duplicate-review.demoQuestion: Can we resolve a verified duplicate while retaining its history and respecting account conflicts?

explanation: The terms can include the recorded price-tier reference and whether the customer must provide a purchase-order reference. Keeping those expectations together helps the counter ask the right questions before an invoice becomes someone else's problem. The owner still reviews and approves the actual arrangement.

Account terms and buyer authority answer different questions. A business having an account does not mean anyone naming that business may charge to it. Review the authorized people, account eligibility and required references alongside the terms so staff understand the whole decision before offering account tender.

capabilities.title: Record the account arrangement
capabilities.text: Retain the supported terms approved for the business customer. This gives staff a shared reference instead of depending on informal explanations that can change between shifts.

capabilities.title: Keep required references clear
capabilities.text: Document the account's purchase-order requirements and relevant price-tier reference. These details help the team understand what needs checking before an eligible charge purchase is completed.

capabilities.title: Separate agreement from authority
capabilities.text: Review who may use the account as a separate part of setup. A recorded customer arrangement should not silently grant every visitor permission to charge purchases to the business.

faq.q: Does creating a trade account automatically authorize all of the company's staff to charge it?
faq.a: No. Authorized buyers are recorded separately with their applicable authority and dates. Account terms describe the business arrangement; they do not establish that every person claiming the company may use it.

faq.q: Does a price-tier reference mean every trade sale automatically receives a discount?
faq.a: Do not assume that. Confirm the supported pricing behaviour and the owner's approved arrangement during setup. A recorded account reference is not a promise of an unverified automatic pricing rule.

trade-account-terms.intro: A landscaping company may buy under a different arrangement from a walk-in shopper. Trade-account terms give the owner a place to record that agreement's supported details, so staff can check the intended account context before completing an eligible trade purchase.

explanation: The buyer's authority has a scope and applicable dates. That matters when crews change, an employee leaves or someone is permitted to make purchases only for a period. Staff need a current, relevant decision rather than a permanent assumption based on a familiar face.

Owners can keep customer service friendly without making account access informal. Review the approved buyer record alongside account status and any required purchase-order details before the charge workflow proceeds. Permission to buy is also distinct from permission to administer the account or change its terms.

capabilities.title: Identify approved people
capabilities.text: Record the individuals eligible to buy against the trade arrangement. This gives the counter a more useful check than accepting that anyone naming a landscaping business speaks for its account.

capabilities.title: Keep dates meaningful
capabilities.text: Review when the recorded authority applies and whether it has expired. A person's previous eligibility should not automatically be treated as present permission for another charge purchase.

capabilities.title: Separate buying from administration
capabilities.text: Keep purchasing authority distinct from account-management access. Someone allowed to collect materials for a crew does not thereby become authorized to change the business's credit terms or setup.

faq.q: Can an expired buyer still charge the account because we recognize them?
faq.a: Recognition does not replace current authority. Review the applicable buyer record and resolve any expired or uncertain permission through the approved account process before accepting an account charge.

faq.q: Does authorizing a buyer give them access to change the account?
faq.a: No. Charging authority and account administration are different responsibilities. Configure the intended buyer permissions without assuming that a permitted purchase grants control over terms, limits or other management decisions.

authorized-trade-buyers.intro: A company name does not tell the cashier who is allowed to charge materials to its account. Authorized trade buyers give that decision a recorded basis, helping staff check the individual in front of them against the business's approved purchasing arrangement.

explanation: This is the customer's reference, not a purchase order your store sends to a grower. Its purpose is to connect the trade purchase with the buyer's business context. The recorded account requirements tell staff when that information needs to be confirmed before the charge workflow continues.

Owners can use this to make trade paperwork less dependent on later phone calls. Staff retain the supplied reference with the relevant sale context, while the customer remains responsible for providing the correct value. A completed field is useful only when it represents the customer's actual purchasing instructions.

capabilities.title: Capture the customer's reference
capabilities.text: Retain the PO or job context supplied for the trade purchase. This helps the record carry information the buyer's accounts team may need when reviewing the resulting invoice.

capabilities.title: Follow account requirements
capabilities.text: Check whether the trade arrangement requires a reference. Staff should understand that requirement before completing the eligible charge workflow rather than discovering a missing detail after the buyer has left.

capabilities.title: Keep buying documents distinct
capabilities.text: Separate the customer's invoice reference from your own supplier purchasing records. Both may be called a PO in conversation, but they describe different commitments and need different context.

faq.q: Is this the same purchase order we use to buy plants from a supplier?
faq.a: No. This is a reference supplied by the business customer for its purchase from your store. Your supplier purchase order belongs to the separate purchasing and receiving workflow.

faq.q: Does the software know whether the customer's reference is commercially correct?
faq.a: Staff must confirm the actual reference provided by the buyer. The account's requirement can guide collection of the information, but the customer's own instructions still determine which reference should be used.
